The repair club · original fictional model

When Dara was younger, he used to throw broken toys away. Last autumn he joined a repair club. One evening he was fixing a wooden train when his neighbour brought in a leather bag with a broken strap.

Dara could not repair the strap alone, so he had to ask an experienced member for help. Now he enjoys learning about different materials. He still makes mistakes, but he keeps trying instead of giving up.

A local film club · original fictional model

Lina has belonged to a film club since 2022. She has helped with several short films, but she has never acted in one. Last month the club entered a local competition and won a small prize.

An interviewer asked Lina if success had changed the group. “We’re pleased,” she said, “but the prize isn’t the most important thing. We’ve made good friends and learned to work together.” Her brother has gone to collect their certificate, so he is not at the meeting now.

A careful rehearsal · original fictional model

The school drama group is preparing a short play. Mira is the student who organizes the costumes, and Eren is the boy who checks the sound equipment. They have a list of props that must be ready before Friday.

Mira thinks one box is too heavy to carry alone. “We should ask for help,” she says. Eren agrees. When she says she is excited about the show, he replies, “So am I.” They decide to rehearse the final scene once more.

The museum performance · original fictional model

A youth group is preparing a short performance at a museum. Their story has a knight, a lost shield and a very nervous messenger. Jaleh has agreed to play the messenger, although she has never acted before.

During rehearsal, she sees two friends carrying a large cardboard castle. She offers to help them. Later the group stops to have a break. Jaleh is tired, but the rehearsal has been exciting, and she feels less frightened about the show.

A workshop changes · original fictional model

An unused room at the youth centre has been turned into a small repair workshop. Last month the tables were cleaned and new shelves were built by volunteers. Broken lamps and toys are now collected there on Fridays.

The volunteers have made a task chart. Items are labelled, checked and placed on the correct shelf. Next month a second room will be opened. Some students feel nervous about explaining the project to visitors, so the group has arranged a practice session.

Agreeing on a meeting · original fictional model

A group of friends wants to make a short film, but they disagree about when to meet. Eda has a music lesson on Friday, and Reza works on Saturday morning. Instead of arguing, they write down the times when everyone is free.

They decide to meet on Saturday afternoon. Eda will text the others as soon as her lesson ends on Friday. If it rains on Saturday, they will use the school hall. Reza goes to the library to borrow a book about filming, and everyone agrees to share the work.

Supplied-edition recording: Mrs Jones describes her own memories and opinions, not a general claim about life today.

When I talk about the time when I was a girl, young people always think that life used to be very hard. But it wasn’t bad really. It was just different and in many ways I think life was better in the past.
Children used to play in the street. They can’t do that now in most places, because everyone’s got a car so there’s too much traffic, and it’s dangerous. Today’s children spend all their free time indoors.
And when I was a girl most people didn’t use to lock their doors.
We didn’t have anything to steal, so it wasn’t a problem.
Of course, we didn’t have a lot of the things that we have today, like computers and mobile phones. But life used to be slower and simpler. People didn’t use to rush around like they do today.
The best thing about the time when I was young was that people used to spend more time together. Nowadays, people spend all their time in front of a computer screen or a television, or on their mobile phones. Yes, in some ways I think life was better when I was young.

We all try to recycle things like glass bottles, drinks cans and plastic bottles. But what happens after you put the things in a recycling box? This is what happens to plastic bottles.
First, plastic bottles are collected from homes.
They are taken to a recycling centre by lorries.
At the centre, the bottles are washed.
Then the clean bottles are cut up into small pieces.
There are lots of different types of plastic, so now the pieces are put into a large tank of water, where they are separated into different kinds of plastic.
The pieces of plastic are heated and melted into a liquid.
The liquid is cooled into long strings.
The strings are dried and then they are chopped into small pellets.
The pellets are sold to factories.
There they are used to make new plastic products.

It was a hot African day and I stopped to have a rest under a tree. I took off my hat and put it down on the ground. Then I lay down and I soon fell asleep. While I was asleep, a monkey took my hat. When I woke up, I put out my hand to pick up my hat, but it wasn’t there. Then I heard a noise in the tree above me. I looked up and I saw the monkey. It was holding my hat. I started to climb up the tree but the monkey just jumped up to a higher branch, so I gave up and climbed down the tree again.
I sat down to think, and I noticed that the monkey sat down, too. I stood up and the monkey stood up, too.
‘Ah-hah,’ I thought. I put my hand in my pocket, took out a handkerchief and put it on my head.
The monkey put on my hat, too. Then I took off the handkerchief, and the monkey took off the hat. Then I threw down the handkerchief on the ground. The monkey threw down my hat.
When the hat landed on the ground, I quickly bent down and picked it up. Then I put it on and walked away. After a while, I looked back. The monkey was still sitting in the tree.
